newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Jan 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Jan 21.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on Jan. 21:

WASHINGTON - William Jefferson Clinton took the oath of office in the last presidential inauguration of the 20th century, urging Americans to bury old racial and political divisions and declaring that the nation stands "on the edge of a bright new prospect in human affairs".

WASHINGTON - If anyone doubted that President Clinton has fixed his sights on the history books, his inaugural address should put that to rest for good. In the last inaugural of the 20th century, Clinton attempted not just to define the future but also to seize the next century as his own.

WASHINGTON - President Clinton triggered shouts of "Amen!" from among the bundled-up, out-of-town crowds when he said that voters did not reelect a Democratic president and a Republican Congress in order to advance the politics of "petty bickering".

WASHINGTON - The important thing this time was to be there, to breathe deeply the air of a historical moment, to see the limos and the escorts and a wonderful parade, to have someone take pictures to show you were present as the president of the United States was inaugurated.
